title: The five integrated elements
blurb: Name the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 Project Management, say what each provides and explain why people matter so much in PRINCE2 Agile.
question: Which list gives the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 Project Management that PRINCE2 Agile builds on?

teach.h: One method, five parts that work together
teach.body: PRINCE2 Project Management is made of five integrated elements: principles, people, practices, processes and the project context. They are 'integrated' because none works alone: principles guide, practices and processes give structure, people apply them, and the project context shapes how. PRINCE2 Agile keeps all five and adds agile ways of working on top.

head: Element
What it gives the project
rows: Seven guiding obligations that make a project PRINCE2
Leadership, teams, culture, communication and change
Aspects (business case to progress) applied all the way through
Activities from pre-project to closure, with responsibilities
Commercial, delivery, organizational and scale factors
teach.caption: Descriptions follow PRINCE2 7 (manual 1.2), on which PRINCE2 Agile V2 builds.

teach.body: PRINCE2 Project Management treats people as a central integrated element: the needs, capabilities and motivations of those who work on the project and those affected by it. PRINCE2 Agile Version 2 strengthens this with a whole people chapter: organizational change management, culture, stakeholders and key influencers, leading teams across organizations and communication.

At Kestrel Mutual, project manager Sanjay Bhatt maps a new claims app to the five elements. The seven principles stay in force (principles). Risk and progress are managed throughout (practices). The work runs from starting up to closing (processes). An external agency and iterative delivery set the scene (project context). And because claims handlers fear the change, he plans coaching and regular demos with them (people).

teach.text: 'Themes' and 'tailoring to the project environment' are 6th edition and Agile V1 language. The Version 2 list is principles, people, practices, processes and the project context. Do not confuse the element 'practices' with the agile techniques (such as stand-ups) that some books also call practices.

items: Five integrated elements: principles, people, practices, processes, project context.
People are central: those working on the project and those affected by it.
PRINCE2 Agile V2 adds a people chapter: OCM, culture, stakeholders, teams, communication.
Four elements, themes and tailoring as an element belong to older versions.

summary: You can now list the five integrated elements and say what each one gives a project. You can also explain why people sit at the centre, and spot outdated lists that use themes or only four elements.

A.q: Which list gives the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 Project Management?
options: Principles, themes, processes, tailoring, project people
Principles, people, practices, processes, project context
Principles, practices, processes, project roles, products
Principles, values, practices, processes, agile mindset
A.why: The five integrated elements are principles, people, practices, processes and the project context (1.3.3).

whyNot.0: Themes and tailoring as an element are older (6th edition) terms.
whyNot.2: Roles and products are parts of practices, not separate elements.
whyNot.3: Values and mindset are layers of the Agile Onion, not PRINCE2 elements.

A.q: Which integrated element covers leadership, teams, culture and communication?
A.why: People is the element covering those working on and affected by the project, including leadership, culture and communication (4.1).

whyNot.0: Practices are aspects such as risk and progress managed throughout.
whyNot.1: Processes are the lifecycle activities from pre-project to closure.
whyNot.3: Principles are the seven guiding obligations.

A.q: Which integrated element includes the commercial setting, delivery method and scale of the project?
A.why: The project context covers commercial, delivery method, organizational and scale factors (1.3.4).

whyNot.1: People covers the humans involved, not these situational factors.
whyNot.2: Practices are the seven aspects such as business case and quality.
whyNot.3: Processes are the activity sets that run the project.

B.q: A training slide lists the PRINCE2 elements as principles, themes, processes and tailoring. What is wrong with it for PRINCE2 Agile Version 2?
options: It should list the seven processes instead
It should show the Agile Onion layers instead
It should add the agile mindset as a sixth element
It is outdated: there are five elements, with practices
B.why: Version 2 builds on PRINCE2 7: five elements (principles, people, practices, processes, project context); themes and tailoring as an element are older terms.

whyNot.0: Processes are one element; listing them does not fix the outdated set.
whyNot.1: The Agile Onion is an agile mindset model, not the PRINCE2 elements.
whyNot.2: There is no sixth element; the agile mindset is part of PRINCE2 Agile guidance.

B.q: Which description fits 'practices' as one of the five integrated elements?
options: Guiding obligations that make a project PRINCE2
Aspects of project management applied throughout
Activities that take a project from start to close
Agile events such as stand-ups and demos
B.why: Practices are aspects of project management (business case, organization, plans, quality, risk, issues, progress) applied throughout the project.

whyNot.3: Stand-ups and demos are agile techniques, not the PRINCE2 practices element.

B.q: How does PRINCE2 Agile Version 2 treat the people element?
options: It leaves people matters to each team's own agile framework
It replaces the people element with the agile mindset
It adds a people chapter on OCM, teams and communication
It treats people as one factor inside the project context
B.why: Version 2 keeps people as a central element and adds content on OCM, culture, stakeholders, leading teams and communication (4.1 to 4.4).

whyNot.0: People is a PRINCE2 element, not left to delivery frameworks.
whyNot.1: The agile mindset supports the people element; it does not replace it.
whyNot.3: People and project context are separate elements.

C.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. People is one of the five integrated elements.
2. Themes are one of the five integrated elements.
3. The project context shapes how principles, practices and processes are applied.
4. Values are one of the five integrated elements.
C.why: People is an element (1), and the project context shapes how the method is applied (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: themes are now practices.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: themes are an older term and values are an Agile Onion layer.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is wrong: values belong to the Agile Onion, not the elements.

C.q: A project manager plans coaching for anxious staff and records that delivery will be iterative by an external agency. Which two elements is she addressing?
C.why: Coaching anxious staff concerns people; iterative delivery by an external agency describes the project context (delivery method and commercial).

whyNot.1: Neither a guiding obligation nor a lifecycle activity is described.
whyNot.2: Coaching is people, but the delivery and supplier facts are context, not a practice.
whyNot.3: The supplier and delivery facts are context, but coaching staff is people, not a process.

C.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The five integrated elements are principles, people, practices, processes and the project [?].
C.why: The fifth element is the project context (1.3.3).

whyNot.0: 'Tailoring to the project environment' was a 6th edition element.
whyNot.1: The project board is a role group within the organization practice.
whyNot.3: The lifecycle is covered by the processes, not a separate element.

reteach.title: A building analogy
reteach.question: How do the five elements fit together?

blocks.body: The principles are the building regulations everyone must follow. The practices are the trades that work across the whole job (electrics, plumbing). The processes are the sequence of the job from survey to handover. The people are the crew and the residents. The project context is the site: its size, the contractor arrangements and the way work is scheduled.

blocks.text: Five, not four. If you see themes or tailoring listed as elements, the source is out of date.

explain.body: Principles, people, practices, processes and the project context (1.3.3). Three of them come in sevens: principles, practices and processes.

test.q: How many integrated elements does PRINCE2 Project Management have?
test.why: There are five: principles, people, practices, processes and the project context.

whyNot.1: Seven is the number of principles, practices and processes.
whyNot.2: Six matches no PRINCE2 7 list; six aspects was the old hexagon.

explain.body: People covers those working on the project and those affected by it, with their needs, capabilities and motivations.

test.q: Whom does the people element cover?
options: The project board members and the PM
Those working on and affected by the project
The delivery teams and their team coaches
The external suppliers working under contract
test.why: People covers both those working on the project and those affected by it.

whyNot.0: The board is part of it, but the element is wider.
whyNot.2: Delivery teams are included, but so are those affected by the change.
whyNot.3: Suppliers may be included, but the element covers everyone involved and affected.

explain.body: Practices are aspects managed all the way through (such as risk). Processes are activity sets used at particular points (such as starting up a project).

test.q: Risk, quality and progress belong to which integrated element?
test.why: Risk, quality and progress are three of the seven practices.

whyNot.1: Processes are activity sets such as 'initiating a project'.
whyNot.2: Principles are guiding obligations such as 'manage by stages'.
whyNot.3: The project context covers commercial, delivery, organizational and scale factors.

explain.body: The setting that shapes how the other elements are applied: commercial arrangements, delivery method, organizational setting and scale.

test.q: Which element would include the fact that a project is part of a programme and uses an external supplier?
test.why: Programme membership and external suppliers are organizational and commercial contexts within the project context.

whyNot.0: Principles are obligations that apply whatever the context.
whyNot.1: People covers those involved and affected, not the commercial setting.
whyNot.3: Practices are aspects managed throughout, such as risk.
